db-resources
Student(StudentID, Name, CourseID) and Course(CourseID, Title): identify primary and foreign keys.
StudentID is the Student primary key. CourseID is the Course primary key and a foreign key in Student. This design assumes each student has one course.
Write SQL to return student names in alphabetical order.

SELECT Name FROM Student ORDER BY Name ASC;
ORDER BY controls display order; storage order is not guaranteed.
A student can take many courses and a course has many students. Redesign the schema.
Student(StudentID PK, Name); Course(CourseID PK, Title); Enrolment(StudentID PK/FK, CourseID PK/FK). The two foreign keys form a composite primary key.
Normalise R(StudentID, CourseID, StudentName, CourseTitle, Mark), key (StudentID, CourseID). State the dependencies.

StudentID determines StudentName; CourseID determines CourseTitle; the complete key determines Mark. Remove partial dependencies into Student and Course. Enrolment(StudentID, CourseID, Mark) keeps the mark. With only these dependencies, all three tables are in 3NF.
Explain why a comma-separated list of course IDs in one cell is unsuitable.

The cell holds several course values, making individual courses hard to validate or join. Store one enrolment per row. 1NF requires one value per attribute in the intended domain, without repeating groups.

Return every student with any matching enrolment using Student(StudentID, Name) and Enrolment(StudentID, CourseID).

SELECT s.StudentID, s.Name, e.CourseID
FROM Student AS s LEFT JOIN Enrolment AS e
ON e.StudentID = s.StudentID;
An unmatched student has NULL in CourseID.
Write a SQL Server constraint limiting Mark to 0 through 100. Explain NULL.

ALTER TABLE Enrolment ADD CONSTRAINT CK_Enrolment_Mark CHECK (Mark BETWEEN 0 AND 100);
CHECK alone permits NULL because the expression is unknown. Use NOT NULL as well when a mark is required.
Write a parameterised SQL Server procedure to select one student.
A transfer subtracts money from one account and adds it to another. What must happen if the second update fails?
Both updates belong in one transaction. Roll back both on failure. Commit only when both succeed. Validate amounts and available balance, and handle concurrent updates.
When could a nonclustered index help? State one cost.
An index on a frequently filtered StudentID may reduce scanning. It uses storage and adds work to inserts, updates and deletes. Inspect the execution plan and realistic data before choosing it.

Advanced Database
Query design, concurrency, distributed data and Hadoop.
advanced-resources
Two users read stock 1 and each sells one item. Explain the bug and a safer update.

Both may believe stock is available. Use an atomic conditional update: UPDATE Product SET Stock = Stock - 1 WHERE ProductID = @id AND Stock > 0; check that exactly one row changed. Group related operations in a transaction.
A query filters on CustomerID but scans a large Orders table. How would you investigate?
Inspect the actual execution plan, row estimates, reads, statistics and parameter values. Consider an index beginning with CustomerID. Compare timings and write costs on representative data.
Explain Hadoop HDFS and MapReduce with a word-count task.
HDFS stores file blocks across machines with replication. Map emits (word, 1). Shuffle groups matching words. Reduce sums each group. A word occurring three times produces (word, 3).
Does a successful backup prove a database can be recovered?
No. Restore it into an isolated environment and validate data and application access. Test recovery time and the acceptable amount of lost work. Protect and retain backups separately.
Compare partitioning and replication.

Partitioning divides data, for example by date, to distribute storage or work. Replication keeps copies to support availability or reads. A distributed system can use both; copies can lag and require consistency decisions.

using var reader = new System.IO.StreamReader("notes.txt"); // Open file
string text = reader.ReadToEnd(); // Read text

Create notes.txt in the working directory first. using releases the file handle when the scope ends, including when an exception occurs. Garbage collection is not a substitute for prompt disposal.
Plan CRUD endpoints for a Student API. Include status codes.

GET /students returns 200 with a list; GET /students/1 returns 200 or 404; POST /students validates input and returns 201 with a Location; PUT /students/1 returns 204 or 404; DELETE /students/1 returns 204 or 404. Invalid input returns 400. Use DTOs and check permissions.
An EF Core update changes a tracked student name. What saves it?

Load the student, check for null, assign student.Name, then await db.SaveChangesAsync(). Register the DbContext and provider first. Keep connection secrets outside source files and use migrations to manage schema changes.
In WPF MVVM, why does changing a property sometimes not update the screen?

The view model must notify binding listeners, usually through INotifyPropertyChanged. Raise PropertyChanged for the property after assigning its backing field. Set DataContext and check the binding path. Commands handle actions without putting business rules in view code.

Explain an image and a container using a school API.
An image is the packaged API and its runtime. A container is a running instance of that image. Several containers can run from one image.
Write commands to build an image and run it on host port 8080.

docker build -t school-api .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 school-api
Run in the folder containing the Dockerfile. The API must listen on container port 8080 and all container interfaces.
Why use a multi-stage Dockerfile for .NET?

Compile and publish in an SDK stage, then copy published files into an ASP.NET runtime stage. This keeps compilers out of the final image and usually reduces its size. Match SDK/runtime major versions to the project.
Inside an API container, does localhost reach a separate database container?

No. localhost means the API container itself. In Compose use the database service name, for example db, and its container port. Both services must share a network. Readiness is separate from startup order.
How do you keep database data and inspect a failing Compose service?

Mount a named volume at the database data directory. Run docker compose logs SERVICE and docker compose ps. Use docker compose down to stop the stack. Adding -v removes named volumes and can delete practice data. Keep passwords in a local ignored environment file or secrets manager.
